text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ECONOMISTUL
- The underground economy accounts for 40 percent of gross domestic product, says Virgil Magureanu, former chief of the Romanian Intelligenece Service in an interview.
- Camenco Petrovici, chairman of the Savings Bank (CEC) says in interview he wants the CEC to remain the bank for small amd medium-sized depositors.
BURSA
- An IMF mission will arrive in Bucharest on Monday to evaluate the state of a stand-by loan and assess the way the government has fulfilled its tasks agreed under the accord.
ADEVARUL ECONOMIC
- Nicolae Staiculescu, state secretary in the Industry Ministry, presents the state and prospects of Romania's mining industry.
- Privatisation must be quickend but rational, says Valentin Ionescu, head of the National Privatisation Agency.
- The newspaper publishes the government decree changing regulations regarding the creation and functioning of commercial companies.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- People aged up to 35 can benefit from low interest credits from the CEC to build or buy houses, says a government decree.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The newspaper publishes a report on Romania's energy policy showing last year it had imported energy worth $2.38 billion.
- Tax evasion in Bucharest in June was worth 3.4 billion lei, said the body responsible for financial propriety.
General:
All newspapers salute U.S. President Bill Clinton who is expected for an eight-hour visit to Bucharest on Friday, the first by a U.S. President in 22 years.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Hungary will open a consulate in the Transylvanian city of Cluj at the end of July.
- The newspaper publishes a full-page report on abandonned children. "Save the Children" association alone is taking care of 500 street children.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The government passed a decree to change the education law and allow ethnic minorities to study in their mother tongue.
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
